source.author: ov
source.text: Eveniunt optata deae: iuvat esse sub undis et modo tota cava submergere membra palude, nunc proferre caput, summo modo gurgite nare, saepe super ripam stagni consistere, saepe in gelidos resilire lacus.
source.text_original: Eveniunt optata deae: iuvat esse sub undis / et modo tota cava submergere membra palude, / nunc proferre caput, summo modo gurgite nare, / saepe super ripam stagni consistere, saepe / in gelidos resilire lacus.
source.text_english: The goddess’s desires are fulfilled: she delights to be beneath the waters and now to submerge all her limbs in the hollow marsh, now to bring her head out and swim only at the surface of the deep pool, often to stand above the bank of the pond, often to spring back into the cold lakes.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: nec vero Odrysius transtris impenditur Orpheus aut pontum remo subigit, sed carmine tonsas ire docet, summo passim ne gurgite pugnent.
reuse.text_original: nec vero Odrysius transtris impenditur Orpheus / aut pontum remo subigit, sed carmine tonsas / ire docet, summo passim ne gurgite pugnent.
reuse.text_english: Nor indeed is Orpheus, son of Odrysius, hung over benches, nor does he drive the sea with an oar; rather, with his song he teaches the shorn oars to go, so that everywhere they do not contend with the top of the wave.
